concept_name: Rotational Kinematics — θ, ω, α and v = ωr
source_book: NCERT Class 11 Physics Ch.7 (System of Particles and Rotational Motion) §7.6-7.7 — table-of-contents scope only, teaching authored from first principles. The atomic claim: rotation is described by three quantities — angle turned θ, turning rate ω, and rate of change of turning α — that obey the SAME equations as straight-line motion (ω = ω₀ + αt is v = u + at with new letters), and v = ωr ties each point's linear speed to the one shared turning rate. Built on the rigid_body_rotation field_3d engine (docs/loop_runs/rotmech/_engine/findings_d.md, the 0c-3 build). Does NOT cover what produces a change in spin (torque, moment_of_inertia — deliberately withheld: the words torque/I never appear anywhere in this concept, Rule 25) or ω as a vector along the axis (angular_momentum). Ships 8 states, not 9: the design's ninth state (calculus slope-of-the-graph beat, a theta(t)/omega(t) graph panel) was ratified DROPPED by founder ruling 2026-08-14 (K6_decision_brief.md) because the graph panel is not yet built chapter-wide — no fallback readout was authored in its place. The design is preserved and the state returns if/when the graph panel lands (revisit_when: graph_panel_lands in curriculum_tags).

real_world_anchor.primary: A ceiling fan after the switch is turned off — it keeps turning and slows at a steady rate.
real_world_anchor.secondary: A bicycle wheel — the rim moves faster than points near the hub.

r.name: Radius of each sliding mass from the axle — fixed for this whole concept, never a slider

m.name: Mass of each of the two symmetric masses — fixed for this whole concept, never a slider

I_frame.name: Fixed inertia of the turntable + rod, excluding the two masses

R_drum.name: Radius where the motor wheel / brake pad contacts the turntable's rim

rod_height_above_pad.name: Vertical clearance of the rod plane above the drum pad plane — apparatus geometry only

theta0.name: Angular reference offset at state entry — the drum stripe's starting position relative to the base start line
theta0.note: Every state authors theta0_rad: 0 — the stripe always starts ON the start line.

omega0.name: Seed angular speed — sets the state's entry ω (guided states) or restarts ω live (explore sandbox)

omega.name: Live angular speed — the derived closed-form quantity, never itself an independent variable or slider
omega.derived: omega(t) = omega0 + alpha_signed * engaged_seconds(t) while a torque source is engaged; constant (holds) once released

theta.name: Live angle turned — the derived accumulated integral of omega; the on-canvas arc draws theta mod 2*pi, the readout shows the full accumulated value
theta.derived: theta(t) = theta(t-h) + omega(t)*h on the engine's fixed 16 ms grid

alpha.name: Angular acceleration readout (guided states) / live control (explore only) — a pure motion reading, never computed from torque/I inside this concept's own definitions
alpha.note: In guided states alpha is a pure READOUT, driven by the authored drive/brake schedule below, never an authored slider. Explore-state control only.

v.name: Live tangential speed of a marked point at radius r_point — derived, its own arrow-length map

r_point_inner.name: S6/explore inner marked point — a paint mark on the rod

r_point_outer.name: S6/explore outer marked point — the mass itself

theta.formula: angle turned, rad — the accumulated integral of omega from state entry; the on-canvas arc shows theta mod 2*pi

omega.formula: angular speed, rad/s — omega(t) = omega0 + alpha*(engaged seconds) while a torque source is engaged; holds constant once released

alpha.formula: angular acceleration, rad/s^2 — the finite difference of omega; +0.60 while the drive is engaged, −0.50 while the brake is engaged, 0.00 with no source engaged or at rest

v.formula: tangential speed of a marked point, m/s — v = omega * r_point

formulas.omega_theta_over_t: ω = θ / t — steady turning; S2's definition of angular speed.
formulas.alpha_delta_omega_over_delta_t: α = Δω / Δt — S3's definition of angular acceleration: how fast ω itself changes. Algebra-only, never d/dt.
formulas.omega_kinematics: ω = ω₀ + αt — S4's equation, algebraically identical to v = u + at with new letters. Valid whenever α is constant over the measured interval.
formulas.theta_kinematics: θ = ω₀t + ½αt² — S7's equation, algebraically identical to x = ut + ½at². Valid whenever α is constant, t measured from the state's own drive-engagement instant.
formulas.v_omega_r: v = ωr — S6's link law: one shared ω, but each point's linear speed scales with its own distance from the axis.

constraints: ω = ω₀ + αt and θ = ω₀t + ½αt² hold exactly whenever α is constant over the measured interval — the same two equations as straight-line kinematics, new letters only.
α is how fast ω itself changes — it is zero for a body spinning at a constant rate (S1/S2/S6), even though ω itself is nonzero and large.
α is signed: positive α speeds the spin up, negative α slows it down. A negative α is still angular acceleration — never narrated as just stopping.
v = ωr — every point of one rigid turntable shares the same ω; each point's linear speed scales with its own radius from the axis.
r = 0.80 m and m = 2.0 kg are fixed constants for this entire concept — no radial slide, no mass change, anywhere, including the explore state.

torque and moment of inertia are never computed, displayed, or narrated inside this concept's own definitions — α is read directly off the motion (a rate of ω), never derived through torque/I (Rule 25).

aha_moment.statement: Rotation's ω = ω₀ + αt is v = u + at with new letters.
aha_moment.visual_confirmation: A chip prints ‘predicted ω = 3.30’ before the wheel even moves; the live ω readout climbs from 1.50 and meets it exactly.

scene_composition.text: The turntable spins steadily; theta is the angle turned from the start line
the stripe starts on the line; the arc grows; the readout counts up from 0.00
each full turn adds 2 pi radians, about 6.28, to the running count

tts_sentences.text_en: This turntable spins at a steady rate.
A start line marks where the angle theta is measured from.
A stripe sweeps a growing arc, and the readout counts the angle turned, in radians.
Each full turn adds two pi radians -- about six point two eight -- to the running count.

STATE_2.title: ω Is Radians Turned Per Second

scene_composition.text: The turntable keeps spinning at the same steady rate
a tick lands every second -- three ticks land equally spaced apart
omega = 1.50 rad/s -- the steady rate the angle grows

tts_sentences.text_en: The turntable keeps spinning at the same steady rate.
A tick lands on the circle every second -- the marks land equally spaced apart.
Equal spacing means the turntable turns through equal angles in equal times.
This steady rate is the angular speed omega -- one point five oh radians per second.

STATE_3.title: α Is How Fast ω Changes

scene_composition.text: A motor wheel moves in and presses onto the turntable's edge
from rest, omega climbs steadily while alpha sits pinned at 0.60
even when omega is barely moving, alpha already reads its full value

tts_sentences.text_en: A motor wheel moves in and presses onto the turntable's edge.
The turntable starts from rest, and its spin rate omega climbs steadily.
The rate at which omega changes is angular acceleration, alpha, steady at zero point six zero radians per second squared.
Even when omega is barely moving, alpha already reads its full value.

scene_composition.text: omega = omega naught + alpha t predicts the answer before the motor even moves
predicted omega = 3.30 prints first -- then the live readout climbs to meet it
just like a car speeding up steadily -- v = u + at, same equation

tts_sentences.text_en: Omega equals omega naught plus alpha t predicts: one point five oh plus zero point six zero times three is three point three oh.
That number prints before the wheel even moves.
The wheel presses on, and the live rate climbs to meet it, just like a car speeding up steadily, same equation, new letters.

scene_composition.text: A brake pad presses onto the turntable's edge
omega falls in a straight line to zero while alpha holds at minus 0.50
like a ceiling fan after the switch is turned off

tts_sentences.text_en: A brake pad presses onto the turntable's edge.
The spin rate omega falls in a straight line to zero, while the angular acceleration alpha holds at minus zero point five zero radians per second squared.
The turntable stops, and alpha returns to zero -- like a ceiling fan after the switch is turned off.

misconception_watch.belief: When the switch goes off, the story is over -- while it slows there is no acceleration.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: The alpha readout sits at minus 0.50 for the entire slow-down while omega falls in a straight line through 1.00, 0.50, to 0.00 -- and the moment omega stops changing, alpha returns to 0.00.
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: Slowing down IS angular acceleration, with a negative sign -- and it lasts exactly as long as the slowing does.

scene_composition.text: Two marks turn together, sharing one turning rate omega
the outer point moves at 1.20 m/s, twice the inner point's 0.60
on a bicycle wheel, the rim moves faster than points near the hub

tts_sentences.text_en: Two marks turn together on the turntable, sharing one turning rate omega.
Yet each point's speed is v equals omega r.
The outer point moves at one point two zero metres per second, twice the inner point's zero point six zero.
On a bicycle wheel, the rim moves faster than points near the hub.

misconception_watch.belief: Every point of a spinning body moves at the same speed.
misconception_watch.visual_counter: Both marked points stay on ONE straight rod line and finish the revolution together (one shared omega) -- while the outer tangent arrow is exactly twice the inner (1.20 vs 0.60 m/s).
misconception_watch.one_line_fix: One turning rate omega for the whole body, but each point's speed is v = omega r.

STATE_7.title: The Angle Grows As t Squared

scene_composition.text: The turntable spins up from rest under the same steady alpha
ticks land at 0.30, 1.20, 2.70 rad -- widening 1 to 3 to 5
theta = omega naught t + one half alpha t squared

tts_sentences.text_en: The turntable spins up from rest under the same steady alpha.
This time, the angle theta grows as t squared: theta equals omega naught t plus one half alpha t squared.
Ticks now land wider apart each second: zero point three zero, zero point nine zero, one point five zero, one to three to five.

scene_composition.text: Everything is yours now
set omega naught, drag alpha -- watch theta, omega, alpha and the speed arrows answer
omega = omega naught + alpha t

tts_sentences.text_en: Now set the starting speed and drag alpha yourself.

regeneration_variants.label: A Record Turntable Spun Up From Rest
regeneration_variants.physical_world: A record turntable sits still. A drive roller presses its rim and the turntable spins up steadily from rest, then holds a constant speed once the roller lifts away.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Identical alpha-as-rate-of-change-of-omega picture: a steady drive gives a constant angular acceleration, and omega = omega0 + alpha t predicts the speed at any instant -- only the labeled object changes.
regeneration_variants.scene_hint: Same turntable rig, same apparatus, same numbers -- the object is relabeled a record turntable instead of a generic rotating platform.

regeneration_variants.label: A Windmill Blade Slowing As the Wind Drops
regeneration_variants.physical_world: A windmill blade spins steadily, then the wind drops and a brake engages -- the blade's turning rate falls in a straight line to rest while its angular acceleration stays negative and constant.
regeneration_variants.same_physics: Same negative-alpha slow-down physics as the concept's brake beat: a constant braking torque gives a constant negative angular acceleration until the body reaches rest, matching the ceiling-fan anchor exactly.
regeneration_variants.scene_hint: Same turntable rig and same numbers -- only the labeled object and narration context change to a windmill blade.
